newsitem.title: USA: Dow snaps record streak as IBM, Boeing rallies fade.
newsitem.headline: Dow snaps record streak as IBM, Boeing rallies fade.

text.p: The Dow industrials snapped an eight-session record streak on Monday as rallies in components IBM and Boeing faded and the market took a time-out from its recent ferocious run-up.

"The market is actually taking a time-out. The broader market is no big deal and there's profit-taking in techs. The market is in a snooze mode," said Alfred Goldman, technical research director at A.G. Edwards.
The Dow slipped one to about 6345. On Friday, the Dow set its eighth straight record and 10th consecutive day of gains.
The blue chip index had soared more than 325 points over the past two weeks before Monday's meager pullback.
Ken Tower, a technical analyst at UST Securities, said the longest string of rising Dow sessions remains the 13 ended January 20, 1987.

As for the broader market, the S&P 500 slipped one to 737 after setting a second straight session of record closing highs on Friday. Losers outpaced gainers 12-11 on active NYSE volume of about 389 million shares.
The tech-studded Nasdaq Composite fell seven to about 1255.

Among Nasdaq technology stocks, bellwether Intel lost 1/2 to 115-3/8, Cisco Systems fell 1-3/8 to 63-3/8 and Applied Materials was off 5/8 to 31-1/4. But Microsoft rose 1-3/8 to 150-3/8, still firming after Wednesday's stock split news.

The Dow had bolted to the day's high of 6376.35 in the afternoon, aided by further strength in IBM and Boeing. IBM rose two to 147, off its session high of 150 after Morgan Stanley raised its 12-month price target to $170 from $145. IBM soared 8-1/8 points Friday to its best finish since before the October 1987 crash.
Boeing rose 1-1/2 to 93-1/4, off its day-high of 94-1/2.

The Pentagon on Saturday said Boeing and Lockheed Martin, up 1-7/8 to 95-5/8, will compete in the final running for the manufacture of the next generation of fighter jets. It awarded Lockheed a $718.8 million contract and Boeing a $661.8 million contract to immediately begin work on their prototypes.

A third team led by McDonnell Douglas was eliminated from the running for the contract that could mean over $170 billion to the eventual winner. McDonnell Douglas slumped 4-1/4 to 52-1/2. Goldman, Lehman and Cowen downgraded the stock.
As for the overall market, Thom Brown, a managing director of Rutherford Brown & Catherwood, said stocks need a pause.
"It desperately needs a rest here. I would expect it to correct over the course of the next week," he said. Brown expects a pullback lasting three to four days. "I don't expect a major downer."

As for special situations, Deutsche Telekom surged 2-39/64 to 21-1/2 in its Wall Street debut. It was part of a $13 billion global share offering in the German phone giant's first stage of privatization, the biggest offering in European history.
Tyco Toys rallied 4-1/2 to 11-1/2 after agreeing to merge with Mattel Inc in a stock deal valued at $755 million.
Mattel said Tyco shareholders would get $12.50 in Mattel stock for each Tyco share. Mattel lost 3/4 to 29-7/8.
Tosco jumped 12-3/8 to 72-1/2 after agreeing to buy Unocal's 76 Products Co for $1.4 billion and the assumption of limited environmental liabilities.Unocal rose 1-1/4 to 40-3/4.

Retailer Donnkenny shed 2-14/16 to 4-3/16, after setting a fresh year-low of four. It warned that results for 1996 would be signficantly below analysts' expectations. Prudential cut the stock to sell and Bear Stearns downgraded the stock to unattractive. The stock has fallen in recent weeks on news Donnkenny's auditors resigned.

Nacco Industries surged 4-5/8 to 47-7/8 after announcing a dutch tender auction to buy back up to 800,000 shares of its outstanding common stock. The company said it would buy the shares back for between $43.50 and $50 each. It had about 8.9 million primary shares outstanding at the end of the third quarter.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 7.23 to 1254.57.
The S&P 500 index fell 0.60 to 737.02.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721.
